To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) image retrieval in compressed domain is a viable alternative to image retrieval in pixel domain; (b) image retrieval in the compressed domain is computationally more efficient than in the pixel domain; and (c), image indexing in compressed domain provides an effective and efficient solution for content based image retrieval.

(a) direct image indexing and retrieving in compressed domain is a viable approach; (b) DCT and wavelet based JPEG are more suitable for content based image indexing and retrieving than JPEG LS; and (c), a new image extraction algorithm is proposed and tested.

(a) content based image indexing and retrieval can be achieved directly in the compressed domains of JPEG, wavelet and JPEG LS, and (b) image extraction can be achieved directly from the compressed JPEG and wavelet domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we index and retrieve images in compressed domain?
the development and evaluation of algorithms for content-based image indexing and retrieval, image extraction, and image retrieval in compressed domain.

the following issues: (a) how to extract image features and content directly in the compressed image domain; (b) how to extract a complete image from compressed domain for content based access; (c) how to index and retrieve images directly in the compressed format; (d) how to improve image retrieval performance in the compressed domain by incorporating image features and content; and (e) how to improve content based image retrieval performance in compressed domain by incorporating pixel domain features.

the image indexing and retrieval can be achieved in compressed domain with a high degree of accuracy, which is as good as or even better than in pixel domain, while the computational complexity is significantly reduced.

the compressed domain is the most promising domain for image indexing and retrieval, as it is more effective and efficient than pixel domain and it is more robust than feature extraction domain.

, the compressed domain image processing is not only a promising research area for future research, but also a very promising area for many practical applications.
